history.dynasty: Bundela (the parikrama path was built by Queen Pratap Kunwari, consort of Maharaja Chhatrasal, in 1725; other accounts credit Bundelkhand kings generally)
history.period: Mythological (Ramayana) origins; existing structures developed over centuries
history.summary: Kamadgiri — 'the mountain that fulfills all desires' — is regarded as the original Chitrakoot, the hill where Lord Rama, Sita and Lakshmana lived during their exile. Legend holds that when Rama performed his father Dasharatha's shraddha here, the gods who attended forgot their departure mantra and stayed on, making the hill their permanent abode. The hill is venerated as the embodiment of Lord Rama himself (Kamtanath, the presiding deity of the whole Chitrakoot region, with Sita as Kamadgiri Devi). A ~5 km circumambulation (parikrama/giri-pradakshina) path encircles the hill, lined with temples including Kamtanath and Bharat Milap; barefoot parikrama is believed to wash away sins and grant wishes. Note: the parikrama path straddles the Madhya Pradesh–Uttar Pradesh border; the Kamadgiri complex is on the Chitrakoot (Satna, MP) side.

name: Kamadgiri Temple
town_description: Chitrakoot is an ancient pilgrimage town spread across the Madhya Pradesh–Uttar Pradesh border, sacred in the Ramayana as the place of Lord Rama's 11-plus years of exile. Its key sites — Kamadgiri, Ram Ghat on the Mandakini river, Hanuman Dhara and Gupt Godavari — draw lakhs of pilgrims, especially on Amavasya days. The MP-side town is Chitrakoot (Satna district), connected by road and rail, with an operational domestic airport at nearby Karwi.

travel.road: Well connected by road via SH-11 to Satna, Prayagraj and Khajuraho
